evidence.role: nuclear-particle bookkeeping precursor grounded in mapped evidence; original wording

hints: Recall the tiny central region of the atom.
Only one of the two named particles carries positive charge.

walkthrough.text: Recall from Lesson 1 that protons and neutrons make up the nucleus.
State that both particles are in the nucleus.
Identify the proton as positively charged.

ai_rubric.observable: States that protons and neutrons are in the nucleus
States that the proton has positive charge

evidence.role: A minus Z neutron-count demand; original values

hints: Nucleon number counts protons and neutrons together.
Subtract proton number from nucleon number.

walkthrough.text: Use neutron number = A - Z.
Calculate 37 - 17 = 20.
Select B.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B, giving 20 neutrons

evidence.role: same-proton-number isotope comparison demand; original options

hints: Compare proton number before nucleon number.
Isotopes keep the element identity but change neutron count.

walkthrough.text: Require the same Z for the same element.
Require different A, hence different neutron counts.
Only option C has Z = 12 for both nuclei and different A values.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects C, identifying equal proton number and different nucleon number

hints: A is the nucleon number.
Nucleons are protons and neutrons.

walkthrough.text: Identify A as nucleon number.
Nucleon number counts all protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Select D.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects D, identifying A as the total number of protons and neutrons

evidence.role: read notation then calculate neutron count; original nuclide

hints: Read the upper-left and lower-left values separately.
Use A - Z only after identifying both values.

walkthrough.text: Read 29 at the lower left as proton number Z.
Read 65 at the upper left as nucleon number A.
Calculate neutron number = 65 - 29 = 36.

hints: The lower-left number is Z and the upper-left number is A.

walkthrough.text: Read the lower-left number as proton number 29.
Read the upper-left number as nucleon number 65.

ai_rubric.observable: States proton number 29
States nucleon number 65

hints: Subtract proton number from nucleon number.

walkthrough.text: Use neutron number = A - Z.
Substitute 65 - 29.
Obtain 36 neutrons and check 29 + 36 = 65.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses neutron number = nucleon number - proton number or substitutes 65 - 29
Obtains 36 neutrons

evidence.role: kg-to-u conversion followed by nuclear bookkeeping; original values

hints: Divide the mass in kilograms by the kilogram value of 1 u.
Carry the whole-number nucleon count into the neutron calculation.

walkthrough.text: Use the nearest whole-number nucleon count A = 60.
Calculate neutrons = 60 - 27 = 33.
Check that 27 protons plus 33 neutrons gives 60 nucleons.

hints: Use mass in u = mass in kg divided by 1.66 × 10^-27 kg u^-1.

walkthrough.text: The powers of ten contribute 10 and 9.96 / 1.66 = 6.
The mass is 60.0 u.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains 60.0 u or 60 u

hints: Treat 60 as A and 27 as Z.

walkthrough.text: Carry A = 60 from part (a).
Calculate A - Z = 60 - 27 = 33.
State 33 neutrons.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses nucleon number 60 and proton number 27 in 60 - 27
Obtains 33 neutrons

evidence.role: mixed prior nuclear-model and current isotope-bookkeeping demand; original particle counts

hints: Use neutrality before nuclear bookkeeping.
For isotope identity, compare proton counts and neutron counts separately.

walkthrough.text: Neutrality gives 15 electrons in each atom because each has 15 positive protons.
Add protons and neutrons: P has A = 31 and Q has A = 33.
Equal Z = 15 makes them the same element; different neutron counts make them isotopes.
Write P as ^{31}_{15}X.

hints: A neutral atom has zero net charge.

walkthrough.text: Each atom has 15 positively charged protons.
Neutrality requires 15 negatively charged electrons in each atom.

ai_rubric.observable: States that P and Q each have 15 electrons
Explains that neutrality requires equal numbers of positive protons and negative electrons

hints: Add protons and neutrons for each nucleus.

walkthrough.text: For P, calculate 15 + 16 = 31.
For Q, calculate 15 + 18 = 33.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains nucleon number 31 for P
Obtains nucleon number 33 for Q

hints: Same element is decided by proton number; isotope difference is decided by neutron number.

walkthrough.text: Both nuclei have proton number 15, so they are the same element.
They have 16 and 18 neutrons, so their neutron numbers differ.
They are isotopes of that element.

ai_rubric.observable: States that P and Q have the same proton number and are therefore the same element
States that P and Q have different neutron numbers and are therefore isotopes

hints: Place A at the upper left and Z at the lower left.

walkthrough.text: Use P's A = 31 and Z = 15.
Place 31 at the upper left and 15 at the lower left of X to write ^{31}_{15}X.

ai_rubric.observable: Writes nuclide notation with 31 at upper left and 15 at lower left of X
